## Data wrangling
```{r, message=FALSE}
# Read three csv files into R
covar  <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
expr   <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
linker <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")

# Rename the blank column header in gene expression file as "PROBEID" to match the 
#gene names file
names(expr)[1] <- "PROBEID"

# Check how many rows
nrow(expr)

# Merge the gene expression file with the linker file
expr_named <- merge(expr, linker, by = "PROBEID")

# Check to see if the number of rows is matching (=500)
nrow(expr_named)

# Convert the new expr_named into a long data
library(tidyverse)
longexprData <- expr_named %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("GSM"),
                      names_to = 'geoID',
                      values_to = 'Expression')

# Merge the long data with covariate data set matching geoID
df <- merge(longexprData, covar, by= "geoID")

sum(is.na(df$Expression))     # should be 0
length(unique(df$geoID))      # should be 157
nrow(df)                      # should be 500 * 157 = 78500

# Spot check that expression values stayed matched to the correct sample
#(a value in the merged data should equal the same cell in the original file)
s <- colnames(expr)[2]        # first sample column
df$Expression[df$PROBEID == 7924712 & df$geoID == s] ==
  expr[expr$PROBEID == 7924712, s]   # TRUE= it matches

# Look at the first 10 rows of df (specify to variables of interest)
head(df[, c("geoID", "GENE", "Expression", "preg_preeclampsia")], 10)
```

## Gene of interest and Variables of interest

(Identify one gene, one continuous covariate, and two categorical covariates of 
interest. At least one categorical variable should be derived from a continuous 
variable)

**Gene:** LIN9 (PROBEID 7924712). LIN9 was selected because it is measured in 
all 157 subjects and varies across them.

**Continuous covariate:** Maternal BMI ("mat_BMI", kg/m²). 

**Two categorical covariates:** 

1. Pregnancy outcome ("preg_preeclampsia"): Preeclampsia vs. Normal.
2. Vitamin D status ("vitD_status"): derived from the continuous variable 
maternal vitamin D ("mat_vitD", ng/mL) using the cutoffs <30 = Insufficient 
and >=30 = Sufficient. (Mirzakhani H, Litonjua AA, McElrath TF, et al. 
Early pregnancy vitamin D status and risk of preeclampsia. J Clin Invest. 
2016;126(12):4702-4715. doi:10.1172/JCI89031)
```{r}
# Remove the text prefix in chosen covariates and change BMI and vit D to numeric
df$mat_BMI  <- as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", df$mat_BMI))
df$mat_vitD <- as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", df$mat_vitD))
df$preg_preeclampsia <- sub(".*: ", "", df$preg_preeclampsia)

# Assign cut offs to vit D status from the continuous variable 
df$vitD_status <- ifelse(df$mat_vitD < 30, "Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)",
                         "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)")
# Filter to the chosen LIN9 gene 
geneData <- df %>% filter(GENE == "LIN9")
# Check the rows (should be 157)
nrow(geneData)
# Check group size and combinations 
table(geneData$vitD_status, useNA = "ifany") 
table(geneData$preg_preeclampsia, geneData$vitD_status) #Match the paper results
```
Finding two additional continuous variables, beside maternal BMI:

1. *Maternal age* (mat_age_yrs), which is a common covariate that would appear in
a Table 1. 

2. *Gestational age at delivery* (delivery_gestAge_wks), which is relevant to 
preeclampsia (often leads to earlier delivery)

```{r}
# Clean the extra prefix in the maternal age variable
df$mat_age_yrs <- sub(".*:","", df$mat_age_yrs)
# Check what type of variable is this
str(df$mat_age_yrs)
# Convert to numeric
df$mat_age_yrs <- as.numeric(df$mat_age_yrs)
# Check if it is numeric now
str(df$mat_age_yrs)

# Repeat the same with gestational age at delivery
df$delivery_gestAge_wks <- sub(".*:","", df$delivery_gestAge_wks)
str(df$delivery_gestAge_wks)
# Convert to numeric
df$delivery_gestAge_wks <- as.numeric(df$delivery_gestAge_wks)
str(df$delivery_gestAge_wks)

# Create the data that is filtered to one gene again so it includes the new 
#cleaned covariates, because otherwise the old geneData still have the two 
#covariates as characters
geneData <- df %>% filter(GENE == "LIN9")

# Use the filtered data (geneData) to check if the new covariates have any NAs
colSums(is.na(geneData[, c("mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks")])) # all 0 :)

```


Define a custom theme that will be applied to the three plots
```{r}
# Define a custom theme
Theme <- theme(# Remove all the extra borders and grid lines
        panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
        # Define the axis
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = rel(1)),
        # element_markdown instead of element_text allow to use *...* to make
        #text italic (which will be used for gene names)
        axis.title.x = element_markdown(color = "black", face = 'bold', size=14),
        axis.title.y = element_markdown(color = "black", face = 'bold', size=14),
        axis.text  = element_markdown(color = "black", face='bold', size=14),
        # Set plot background
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        # Set the legend
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        legend.text= element_markdown(color= "black", face='bold', size=13),
        legend.title= element_markdown(color= "black", face='bold', size=13),
        # Move legend to the top
        legend.position = 'top',
        # Set the plot title color and make it centered 
        plot.title = element_markdown(color = "black", 
                                  face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5))

```

## Generate a histogram of gene expression of my chosen gene "LIN9"
```{r}
# Install ggtext to italicize text later
#install.packages("ggtext")
# Load ggtext 
library(ggtext)
# Compute a histogram with geom_histogram, set the x axis to gene expression
ggplot(geneData, aes(x=Expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins= 15, fill= "steelblue", color="white") +
  # Change labels (the *...* make the gene name italic)
  labs (x= paste0("*LIN9* Expression"), 
        y= "Number of Subjects",
        title= paste0("Distribution of *LIN9* Expression")) +
  # Set the theme to the custom theme
  Theme
```

## Generate a scatterplot of Covariate vs. Gene Expression using the continuous covariate (BMI) and the LIN9 expression. 
```{r}
# Compute a scatter plot using ggplot and the custom theme 
ggplot(geneData, aes(x = mat_BMI, y = Expression)) +
  # Add scatter plot and define colors
  geom_point(color= "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Add regression line
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color= "black", formula = y ~ x) +
  # Change labels
  labs(x = expression(bold("Maternal BMI (kg/m"^2*")")),
       y = '*LIN9* Expression',
       title = "*LIN9* Expression vs Maternal BMI") +
  # Set the theme to the custom theme
  Theme
```

## Generate a boxplot of Gene Expression separated by both categorical variables
```{r}
# Compute a box plot using ggplot and the custom theme
ggplot(geneData, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = Expression, fill = vitD_status)) +
  # Add boxplot (hide outlier dots because every subject is plotted below)
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Overlay each subject as a jittered point to show the sample size per group
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2,
                                             dodge.width = 0.75,
                                             seed = 103),
             size = 1.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Define colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)" = "hotpink",
                               "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)"  = "skyblue")) +
  # Change labels
  labs(x = "Pregnancy Outcome", y = "*LIN9 Expression*", fill = "Vitamin D Status",
       title = "*LIN9* Expression by Pregnancy Outcome\nand Vitamin D Status") +
  # Put the legend on two rows so the full labels fit
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  # Set the theme to the custom theme
  Theme
```

## Generate a function to produce the submission 1 plots and new plots for the two
additional genes
```{r}
# Function to produce histogram, scatterplot, and boxplot for each gene
buildPlots <- function(data, geneList, contVar, catVars, contLabel = contVar, 
                       catLabels = catVars) {
  # Loop through each gene in the geneList
  for (gene in geneList) {
    # Subset to one current gene
    geneData <- data[data$GENE == gene,]
    
    # Add histogram of gene expression
    plot1 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = Expression)) +
      # 15 bins used because it is shows the shape clearly for 157 subjects
      geom_histogram(bins=15, fill= "steelblue", color = "white") +
      # paste0() puts the current gene name into the labels, and *...* italicize
      #the gene name
      labs(x = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression"), y = "Number of Subjects", 
           title = paste0("Distribution of *", gene, "* Expression")) +
      # Apply the custom theme
      Theme
    # Display the plot
    print(plot1)
    
    # Add scatterplot of the continous covariate vs expression
    # x = .data[[contVar]] reads the column whose name is stored in the string, 
    #since x= contVar will plot the text itself
    plot2 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = .data[[contVar]], y = Expression)) +
    # alpha=0.7 makes overlapping points visible
      geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      # Avoid a console message by adding formula = y~x
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", formula = y ~ x) +
      # Set up the axis titles, gene expression
      labs(x = contLabel, y = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression"),
           title = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression vs ", contLabel)) +
      # Apply theme
      Theme
    # Print the second plot 
    print(plot2)
    
    # Add boxplot by both categorical covariates with jittered points
    plot3 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = .data[[catVars[1]]], y = Expression,
                               fill = .data[[catVars[2]]])) +
      # Hide the plot's own outliers because all subjects are plotted below and 
      #outliers would be drawn twice otherwise (this was pointed out by Claude when
      #using it to check my function)
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
      # Add jitter (this function is helped by Claude)
      geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2,
                                                 dodge.width = 0.75,
                                                 # set seed so jitters are the 
                                                 #same each time
                                                 seed = 103),
                 size = 1.8, alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("hotpink", "skyblue")) +
      labs(x = catLabels[1], y = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression"), fill = catLabels[2],
           title = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression by ", catLabels[1],
                          # break the title into two lines (this function is helped
                          # by Claude)
                          "<br>and ", catLabels[2])) +
      # put legends on two rows so full labels can fit
      guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
      Theme
    print(plot3)
  }
}
```

## Call the function for each gene
```{r}
# Print the 9 plots using the function
buildPlots(data = df,
           geneList = c("LIN9", "UTS2", "RUNDC3A"),
           contVar = "mat_BMI",
           catVars = c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitD_status"),
           contLabel = "Maternal BMI (kg/m\u00b2)",
           catLabels = c("Pregnancy Outcome", "Vitamin D Status"))
```
